text:
"But what can you actually do for me?"

Fair question. Here's my plain answer.

I get you found when people search for what you do.
Then I keep you showing up until they're ready to call.

Two jobs. One system.
More calls. More enquiries. More booked jobs.

One company promises top three on Google in 90 days. Another says 6 to 12 months.

Google's own video on hiring an SEO says it usually takes four months to a year to make changes and see the benefit.

I'd trust the longer quote. They've done the work before.

A builder in Baldivis asked me what I'd actually do for him.

So I searched "home builder Baldivis" on his phone.
Competitors on the map. Competitors in the ads. Him nowhere.

Step one, get him there.
Step two, keep him in front of those people until they're ready to sign.

How fast you climb the Google map comes down to where you start.

An electrician in Ballarat with a half-filled profile and three rivals can move quick.
A dentist in Bondi Junction up against forty clinics takes longer.

Anyone quoting a timeline before looking is guessing.

Two-minute check if you run Google Ads:

Open Change history. See who made the last few changes.

If it was Google, or nobody's touched it in months, your account is on autopilot.

A set-and-forget account is the most expensive kind.

Worth checking this week.

Your phone updates itself overnight. You wake up with a new lime emoji.

You don't need to know why the lime exists. You just need it to make calls.

Google Ads works the same way. Most updates won't touch a local business. The few that do can quietly cost you money.
